info.name: Auth0 Authentication actions Authorize User API
Auth0 Authenticate a User with a Social Provider, Database/AD/LDAP (Passive), SAML/Windows Azure AD (Passive), Authorization Code Flow, Authorization Code Grant (PKCE) Flow, or Implicit Flow

params.name: audience
params.description: The unique identifier of the target API you want to access

params.name: scope
params.description: The scopes which you want to request authorization for. These must be separated by a space. You can request any of the standard OpenID Connect (OIDC) scopes about users, such as profile and email, custom claims that must conform to a namespaced format, or any scopes supported by the target API (for example, read:contacts). Include offline_access to get a Refresh Token.

params.name: response_type
params.description: Indicates to Auth0 which OAuth 2.0 flow you want to perform. Use code for Authorization Code Grant Flow, token for Implicit Flow, or id_token token for both an ID Token and an Access Token.

params.name: redirect_uri
params.description: The URL to which Auth0 will redirect the browser after authorization has been granted by the user.

params.name: state
params.description: An opaque value the applications adds to the initial request that the authorization server includes when redirecting the back to the application. This value must be used by the application to prevent CSRF attacks.

params.name: nonce
params.description: A string value which will be included in the ID Token response from Auth0, used to prevent token replay attacks. It is required for response_type=id_token token.

params.name: code_challenge_method
params.description: Method used to generate the challenge. The PKCE spec defines two methods, S256 and plain, however, Auth0 supports only S256 since the latter is discouraged.

params.name: connection
params.description: The name of the connection configured to your application.

params.name: prompt
params.description: To initiate a silent authentication request, use prompt=none.

params.name: organization
params.description: ID of the organization to use when authenticating a user. When not provided, if your application is configured to Display Organization Prompt, the user will be able to enter the organization name when authenticating.

params.name: invitation
params.description: Ticket ID of the organization invitation. When inviting a member to an Organization, your application should handle invitation acceptance by forwarding the invitation and organization key-value pairs when the user accepts the invitation.

items.docs:
Use this endpoint to authenticate a user. The following flows are supported:
  - Social Provider Authentication
  - Database/AD/LDAP (Passive) Authentication
  - SAML/Windows Azure AD (Passive) Authentication
  - Authorization Code Flow
  - Authorization Code Grant (PKCE) Flow
  - Implicit Flow
